maria: Quick bug report — python SDK async tool-calling + structured output seems broken for me. When I use the `functions` param and expect a parsed structured output (dict/TypedDict), I get a raw JSON string instead of the parsed object. :bug:

maria: Minimal repro (async):
```py
from redwood import AsyncClient
from typing import TypedDict

class UserInfo(TypedDict):
    name: str
    age: int

client = AsyncClient(api_key=...)

resp = await client.chat.completions.create(
    model="gpt-4-rw",
    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Provide user info"}],
    functions=[{
        "name": "user_info",
        "parameters": {"type": "object", "properties": {"name": {"type": "string"}, "age": {"type": "integer"}}}
    }],
    function_call={"name": "user_info"}
)

# I expect resp.choices[0].message.function_call.arguments to be a dict matching UserInfo
print(type(resp.choices[0].message.function_call.arguments))  # -> <class 'str'>
print(resp.choices[0].message.function_call.arguments)
```

maria: SDK version: 0.8.2, python 3.11. Behavior observed both on hosted and local dedicated.

alex: Repro'd locally, thanks for the clear snippet. I see the same — we parse the tool call payload but we don't run json.loads in the async path for some reason. Sync client does fine. :eyes:

sam: Might be related to recent typing changes around FunctionCall object. We changed the pydantic model to keep raw args as str to preserve whitespace, but we forgot the helper that returns parsed args as `.arguments_parsed` or similar.

maria: Ah—interesting. In the sync API we used to have message.function_call.arguments as dict in v0.7.x, right? I upgraded to 0.8 and hit this. Any recommended workaround?

alex: Temporary workaround: json.loads(resp.choices[0].message.function_call.arguments) manually. Ugly but works.

sam: Filed a quick GH issue and assigned to alex: https://github.com/redwood-inference/py-sdk/issues/678

alex: Plan: add an opt-in parsing flag on the AsyncClient constructor (parse_function_arguments=True by default), fix the async deserializer to call json.loads when the payload looks like JSON, and add typing helpers so typing users get a TypedDict-friendly object. Will open a PR later today.

maria: Nice. Two asks from my side: 1) keep the behavior configurable (some users rely on raw string). 2) Add a small doc example showing how to cast/validate into a TypedDict or pydantic model.

sam: Agreed. Also add a unit test that simulates chunked streaming (async) because this might be due to how streaming pieces get joined.

ci-bot: CI queued for branch fix/async-func-arg-parse (runs: unit, integration)

alex: FYI I found a second async-only bug: when awaiting client.tools.invoke(...) if the tool returns structured JSON and the SDK raises a JSONDecodeError we currently drop the original error context. I'll handle both in the same PR.

maria: Thanks — do you mind adding a short sample in examples/async_tool_call.py? I can pick it up if you're busy.

alex: I can add the core fix + tests. If you want to add the example, that'd be great, otherwise I'll add a minimal one.

maria: I'll add the example and a tiny note in the migration guide about the change in 0.8.x -> 0.9.0 behavior.

sam: Punted to milestone 0.9.0. Tagging: DX, python-sdk, async, tool-calls.

maria: Thanks everyone. Leaving the manual workaround in our internal guide for now. :+1:

alex: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/py-sdk/pull/1234 — fixes async parse and adds parse flag + tests. Please review.

sam: Reviewing now. If green, we'll include in the next patch.

maria: Verified locally with alex's branch; parsed object is back and typing feels better. Great work :rocket:
